claim.quote: The PICASSO collaboration observed for the first time a significant difference between the acoustic signals induced by neutrons and alpha particles in a detector based on superheated liquids.

name: Discrimination of nuclear recoils from alpha particles with superheated liquids
notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 10 Jul 2008); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v2, last revised 23 Sep 2008).

summary.plain: PICASSO found that alpha particles and neutrons make different sounds when they pop a droplet, which gives a new way to tell alpha background from nuclear recoils.
summary.technical: Acoustic signals of alpha-induced and neutron-induced nucleations differ in superheated C4F10; the abstract attributes the effect to multiple bubbles forming on alpha tracks versus single nucleations from neutron recoils.

title: Discrimination of nuclear recoils from alpha particles with superheated liquids
why_it_matters: The abstract says the effect offers the possibility of improved background suppression for dark matter experiments.
